title: Exceptional inverse image of a smooth morphism commutes with extension of coefficients
statement:
Work in the standing scheme setting [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]: $k$ has characteristic $p>0$, $\ell\ne p$ is prime, and $X,Y$ are separated finite-type $k$-schemes. Let $f:X\to Y$ be smooth of pure relative dimension $d\geq0$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Fix its coefficient-independent compactification. Let $A\to B$ be a unital map of finite commutative rings, each annihilated by a power of $\ell$. Write $\Dctf(T_{\mathrm{proét}},R)$ for complexes of sheaves of modules over the constant ring sheaf $R_T$ with bounded constructible cohomology and finite Tor amplitude [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf, def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude]. Use derived coefficient extension $K_B=K\otimes^L_{A_T}B_T$ [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor], the constructible adjunctions $Rf_{!,R}\dashv f_R^!$ for $R=A,B$ [sk-prop-sf-rf-shriek-preservation], and the canonical compact-support comparison $b$ [det-sp-reduction-direct-image]. For a common annihilator $N=\ell^n$ of $A,B$, the Tate line is the inverse image from the etale site of $\mu_{N,T}\otimes_{(\mathbf Z/N)_T}R_T$; write $K(d)=K\otimes^L_R R_T(1)^{\otimes d}$ [def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist].

For
$K\in\Dctf(Y_{\mathrm{proét}},A)$ let

$$
c_{A,B}(K):(f_A^!K)_B\longrightarrow f_B^!(K_B)\quad\text{in }\Dctf(X_{\mathrm{proét}},B)
$$

be the unique morphism (the transpose under $Rf_{!,B}\dashv f_B^!$) satisfying

$$
\varepsilon_B(K_B)\circ Rf_{!,B}\bigl(c_{A,B}(K)\bigr)
=(\varepsilon_A(K))_B\circ b(f_A^!K)^{-1}.
$$

Then $c_{A,B}(K)$ is natural in $K$ and is an isomorphism. On a coordinate
chart $f|_U=p_d\circ e$ (with $e:U\to\mathbf A^d_Y$ étale and $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ is the chart inclusion, where
$j^*f_A^!\simeq e^*p_d^*(-)(d)[2d]$ is the counit-preserving identification for the chart adjunction whose counit is summation over the fibres of $e$ followed by the affine-space counit of [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace], transported from the etale site) it is the canonical isomorphism
$(e^*p_d^*K(d)[2d])_B\simeq e^*p_d^*(K_B)(d)[2d]$.

proof.text: Put $T_X=(-)_B$, $T_Y=(-)_B$, $F_R=Rf_{!,R}$ and $G_R=f_R^!$. By [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor](1),(2), $T_X,T_Y$ preserve the indicated categories. By [sk-prop-sf-rf-shriek-preservation], $F_R\dashv G_R$ is an adjunction on them. Applying [det-sp-reduction-direct-image] to $G_AK$ gives the natural isomorphism $b(G_AK):T_YF_AG_AK\to F_BT_XG_AK$. Thus $\tau_K=T_Y(\varepsilon_A(K))b(G_AK)^{-1}$ is a well-typed map $F_BT_XG_AK\to T_YK$, with no flatness requirement on $B$ over $A$.

Under the adjunction of [sk-prop-sf-rf-shriek-preservation], define $c_K$ to be the transpose of $\tau_K$. The inverse transpose of $h:T_XG_AK\to G_BT_YK$ is $\varepsilon_B(T_YK)F_B(h)$. Hence its counit identity is exactly the displayed identity in the statement, and this identity determines $c_K$ uniquely. For $u:K\to L$, naturality of $b$ [det-sp-reduction-direct-image] and of $\varepsilon_A$ gives $T_Y(u)\tau_K=\tau_LF_BT_XG_A(u)$. Naturality of $\varepsilon_B$ identifies the left side with the inverse transpose of $G_BT_Y(u)c_K$ and the right side with the inverse transpose of $c_LT_XG_A(u)$. Injectivity of the hom bijection proves naturality of $c$.

source.place: Existence, uniqueness, naturality: transpose and its naturality

proof.text:
For any scheme $T$ used below and $R=A,B$, the finite ring $R$ is discrete Noetherian: every ascending chain of ideals stabilizes since the underlying set is finite. The scheme $T$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], hence qcqs. Apply [det-pe-finite-tor-comparison-noetherian]: $
u_T^*$ is an equivalence on the bounded constructible finite-Tor categories, preserving and reflecting every Tor interval. Thus its stated conclusion supplies exactly the finite-Tor equivalence needed by [det-sp-et-proet-adjunction-transfer], for arbitrary finite rings, not just DVR quotients. Comparison inverse image is exact and carries constant rings to constant rings by [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact]; its tensor comparison is [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. These comparisons identify coefficient extension and the pullback, Tate-tensor and shift functors on the two sites. The Tate sheaves are locally free of rank one by [lem-asd-finite-etale-twist-line]. The ordinary compact-support functor also restricts to these subcategories. Indeed its value $F^{\mathrm{et}}L$ on bounded input is bounded below, since it is $Rr_*j_!L$ with $j_!$ exact. The site comparison of [lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility] identifies $
u^*F^{\mathrm{et}}L$ with $F
u^*L$, which is in $\Dctf$ by [sk-prop-sf-rf-shriek-preservation]. Choose bounded constructible etale origin $M$ for this object using [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-constructible-derived-origin]. Full faithfulness on $D^+$ [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] lifts the isomorphism $
u^*F^{\mathrm{et}}L\simeq
u^*M$ to $F^{\mathrm{et}}L\simeq M$. The Tor reflection already cited then gives $F^{\mathrm{et}}L\in\Dctf$.

source.place: Charts: finite-Tor comparison and tensor identifications

proof.text:
We compute the ordinary-etale chart adjunction in Steps 7–11 and then transport it. Its right functor $H_{g,R}=e^*p_d^*(-)(d)[2d]$ restricts to the finite-Tor constructible categories: after $
u^*$ it is the pro-etale pullback followed by a locally trivial rank-one tensor and a shift. Pullback preserves $\Dctf$ by [det-proper-base-change-unbounded-pullback], with the finite-ring module-object/ordinary-module identification of [sk-prop-sf-rf-shriek-preservation]; rank-one tensor is locally the identity, and shifts preserve boundedness and translate Tor intervals. The equivalence of Step 3 reflects this membership. The specified site comparison $c_{g,R}:
u_Y^*F^{\mathrm{et}}_{g,R}\simeq F_{g,R}
u_U^*$ is an isomorphism by [lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility]. Consequently [det-sp-et-proet-adjunction-transfer] identifies the transported right adjoint with $g_R^!$, retaining the actual counit
$$\epsilon^{\mathrm{pro}}_{g,R}=
u_Y^*(\epsilon^{\mathrm{et}}_{g,R})c_{g,R}^{-1}.$$
The first square and its following counit clause in [lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility] carry a coefficient-counit identity with the ordinary-etale $ eta_g$ to that same identity with the named pro-etale $b_g$. We use that precise assertion in Step 11, so the transported comparison is the fixed-compactification map of the statement.

source.place: Charts: transport of the specified adjunction and coefficient-counit equation

proof.text: For $q:\mathbf P^1_S\to S$ over any base chart in our setting, choose $N=\ell^n$ annihilating both rings and put $R_0=\mathbf Z/N$. The bases and projective lines are Noetherian and $N$ is invertible; Noetherianity follows from [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. By [lem-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-adjunction], for $R=A,B$ the splitting $s_R:R_S(1)[2]\oplus R_S\xrightarrow{\sim}Rq_*R_{\mathbf P^1_S}(1)[2]$ has components the shifted unit and the scalar-extended Kummer class $h_R$. More precisely, the cited statement defines $h_R$ by first taking the Kummer class over $R_0$, extending scalars to $R$ on $\mathbf P^1_S$, and then applying inverse-image/direct-image adjunction. Write $H_0:(R_0)_{\mathbf P^1_S}\to(R_0)_{\mathbf P^1_S}(1)[2]$ for that Kummer morphism. Then $H_R=H_0\otimes^L_{R_0}R$ has adjunct $h_R$. Derived tensor associativity gives $(H_0\otimes^L_{R_0}A)\otimes^L_AB=H_0\otimes^L_{R_0}B$, with the canonical identifications of both endpoints; hence $(H_A)_B=H_B$. Step 6 checks the corresponding direct-image equality with the named coefficient map by transposition.

source.place: Charts: common exponent and scalar-extended Kummer class

proof.text:
On the ordinary etale site put $b_q=\beta_q^{\mathrm{et}}$, the proper comparison explicitly defined and asserted invertible in [lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility], evaluated on $A_{\mathbf P^1_S}(1)[2]$. The source twist is locally free of rank one by [lem-asd-finite-etale-twist-line]. Thus its derived scalar extension is ordinary tensor and is canonically $B_{\mathbf P^1_S}(1)[2]$: on an etale trivialization the map is $A\otimes_A B\to B$, $a\otimes b\mapsto ab$, and these maps respect the transition units of $\mu_N$. On the two components of the splitting of Step 5 the comparison sends the unit to the unit and $(h_A)_B$ to $h_B$. For the unit this follows from the defining counit-transpose projection map: its composite with the pullback/direct-image unit is the coefficient-extended unit, by the adjunction triangle identity; for the second component, take the inverse transpose of $b_q(h_A)_B$ under $q_B^*\dashv Rq_{*,B}$. The defining counit identity for $b_q$ and naturality give $(\epsilon_{q,*,A}\,q_A^*h_A)_B=(H_A)_B=H_B$, where $\epsilon_{q,*,A}$ is the ordinary pullback/direct-image counit, not the exceptional counit. The inverse transpose of $h_B$ is also $H_B$ by definition; injectivity of this hom bijection gives $b_q(h_A)_B=h_B$. Thus $b_q(s_A)_B=s_B$. By [def-amb-p1-trace], $t_{q,R}=\operatorname{pr}_2s_R^{-1}$. Multiplying the preceding equality by inverses gives
$$t_{q,B}\,b_q=(t_{q,A})_B.$$
Indeed both composites with $(s_A)_B$ are the projection onto the second summand. This is a two-component calculation with an invertible splitting, not an extra lemma asserting the desired exceptional comparison.

source.place: Charts: scalar extension of the projective-line splitting and trace

proof.text:
The actual projective-line counit is $\epsilon_{q,R,K}=(1_K\otimes t_{q,R})\pi_R^{-1}$ with the tensor unit constraint, by [lem-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-adjunction] and [def-amb-p1-trace]. Put $L_R=R_{\mathbf P^1_S}(1)[2]$ and $F_R=Rq_{*,R}$, so $G_{q,R}K=q_R^*K\otimes_R^L L_R$. The canonical tensor/pullback comparison is [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Apply the square of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-exchange-tensor-coherence] to the ringed-topos square with scheme maps $q,q$ and coefficient change $A\to B$. After its canonical tensor and symmetry identifications, the square says exactly
$$
F_B(a_{q,K})\,b_q(G_{q,A}K)\,(\pi_A)_B
=\pi_B\,(1_{K_B}\otimes b_q(L_A)),
$$
where $a_{q,K}:(q^*K(1)[2])_B\xrightarrow{\sim}q^*(K_B)(1)[2]$. Both sides start at $K_B\otimes_B^L(F_AL_A)_B$ and end at $F_BG_{q,B}(K_B)$. Compose with $\epsilon_{q,B,K_B}=(1\otimes t_{q,B})\pi_B^{-1}$. The right side becomes $1_{K_B}\otimes(t_{q,B}b_q(L_A))=1_{K_B}\otimes(t_{q,A})_B$ by Step 6; this is $(\epsilon_{q,A,K})_B(\pi_A)_B$. Here $K$ ranges over $\Dctf(S_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, the only inputs used in Steps 9–11: then $G_{q,A}K=q^*K\otimes^L_AL_A$ is again bounded constructible of finite Tor amplitude (pullback, a locally free rank-one twist [lem-asd-finite-etale-twist-line] and a shift), so $b_q(G_{q,A}K)$ is an isomorphism by [lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility]; $\pi_A$ is invertible because the counit of [lem-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-adjunction] is written with $\pi^{-1}$. Since $(\pi_A)_B$ and $b_q(G_{q,A}K)$ are isomorphisms, cancellation gives
$$
(\epsilon_{q,A,K})_B\,b_q(G_{q,A}K)^{-1}
=\epsilon_{q,B,K_B}\,Rq_{*,B}(a_{q,K}).
$$
Thus the actual counit at every $K\in\Dctf(S_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ has the required coefficient identity (the uninverted form $\epsilon_{q,B,K_B}Rq_{*,B}(a_{q,K})b_q(G_{q,A}K)=(\epsilon_{q,A,K})_B$ holds for every $K$). This argument uses no flatness of $B$ over $A$.

source.place: Charts: projective-line counit at an arbitrary complex

proof.text:
For an open immersion $j$ or a separated finite-type etale chart map $e$, use the exact sum-extension adjunction [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality]. Its derived coefficient comparison is the summandwise tensor identification $\sigma_e$ specified by [lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility]. Compute its counit before passage to the derived category. The direct-sum presheaf [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension] and its geometric-fibre description [lem-amb-etale-sum-stalks] give the evaluation map $\bigoplus_x M_x\to M$, $(m_x)\mapsto\sum_xm_x$. On every summand the two coefficient-extended evaluations agree because
$$ (\sum_xm_x)\otimes b=\sum_x(m_x\otimes b). $$
This is equality of the sheaf maps induced from the presheaf sums; it is not a test for equality of arbitrary derived morphisms on stalks. The same degreewise equality on the K-flat representatives computing $\sigma_e$ gives
$$\epsilon_{e,B}\,De_{!,B}(a_e)=T(\epsilon_{e,A})\sigma_e(e_A^*-)^{-1},$$
where $a_e:T e_A^*\simeq e_B^*T$ is the canonical pullback/tensor comparison. The open case is the same formula with at most one lift. No flatness of $B$ over $A$ is needed.

source.place: Charts: scalar compatibility of sum-extension counits

proof.text:
Use clause (2) of the existing Mathlib leaf [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] for the two consecutive chart adjunctions $F_{i,R}\dashv G_{i,R}$, $i=1,2$, with coefficient functors $T_0,T_1,T_2$. The square at stage $i$ is $b_i^{-1}:F_{i,B}T_{i-1}\to T_iF_{i,A}$. Its mate is $a_i:T_{i-1}G_{i,A}\to G_{i,B}T_i$, precisely because its counit equation is the identity checked in Steps 7 and 8. Put
$$ b_{12}=F_{2,B}(b_1)b_2(F_{1,A}-),\qquad a_{12}=G_{1,B}(a_2)a_1(G_{2,A}-). $$
Clause (2) states that $a_{12}$ is the mate of the pasted square $b_{12}^{-1}$ for the composite adjunction of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. Taking its inverse transpose therefore gives
$$\epsilon_{12,B}F_{2,B}F_{1,B}(a_{12})=T_2(\epsilon_{12,A})b_{12}(G_{1,A}G_{2,A}-)^{-1}.$$
This applies an existing general composition theorem instead of hiding a separate lemma with its own adjunction hypotheses in the chart calculation.

source.place: Charts: mates of the two consecutive adjunction squares

proof.text: Apply Step 9 first to the open-extension adjunction for $\mathbf A^1_S\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^1_S$ and the projective-line adjunction from Step 7. This gives the required coefficient-counit identity for the affine-line adjunction. By [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace], the $d$-coordinate adjunction is the ordered composite of these affine-line adjunctions. Its $d=0$ case is the identity, where both comparisons are identities; if the identity holds for $d$, apply Step 9 with one further affine-line factor to obtain it for $d+1$. Tensor associativity and pullback monoidality of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] identify the resulting $a_{12}$ with $(p_d^*K(d)[2d])_B\simeq p_d^*(K_B)(d)[2d]$. The left-functor composition isomorphism is supplied by [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons]. The composition square of [lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility] identifies $b_{12}$ with the named compact-support coefficient map after that isomorphism; its refinement square makes this true for the chosen compactification as well. Thus induction proves the identity with the specified $b_{p_d}$, not just an unspecified isomorphism between its endpoints.

source.place: Charts: affine-line restriction and coordinate induction

proof.text:
On a chart $g=fj=p_de$ the composite adjunction of Steps 8–10 has right adjoint $H_{g,R}K=e^*p_d^*K(d)[2d]$ and composite counit, by [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] and the etale adjunction [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality]. After the counit-preserving left-functor identifications below, the restriction isomorphism $j^*G_R\simeq G_{g,R}$ of [det-sf-mate-open-restriction] identifies it with this right adjoint by the counit-preserving uniqueness of right adjoints. Apply the coefficient identities of Steps 7–10 and the transport of Step 4. With $a_{g,K}:(H_{g,A}K)_B\xrightarrow{\sim}H_{g,B}(K_B)$ they give precisely
$$ (\epsilon_{g,A,K})_B\,b_g(H_{g,A}K)^{-1}
=\epsilon_{g,B,K_B}\,Rg_{!,B}(a_{g,K}). $$
This constructs the chart adjunction for arbitrary finite $A,B$ from existing general finite-ring projective-line and etale adjunctions; the narrower $\mathbf Z/\ell^n$ chart lemma is not applied to an arbitrary finite ring. The left adjoint of this composite is $Rp_{d!}\circ De_{\Sigma!}$; by [lem-asd-etale-compact-support-normalization] the identification $c_e:Re_!^c\simeq De_{\Sigma!}$ carries the compact-support adjunction of $e$ to $De_{\Sigma!}\dashv e^*$ with its sum/evaluation counit, so composing with the composition map $\alpha$ identifies the chart left adjoint with $Rg_!$, counits included. The etale normalization square of [lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility] says that under $c_e$ the coefficient map $\beta_e^c$ is the summandwise tensor identification used for $e$ in Steps 8–10. Apply the composition and refinement squares of [lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility] to the compactifications of $e$, $p_d$ and $g=p_de$. They identify the coefficient map used in the composite chart counit with $b_g$ for the chosen compactification. Hence the displayed counit identity uses exactly the map defining the transpose $c_{g,K}$.

source.place: Charts: counit identity for the complete coordinate chart

proof.text:
The comparison $c_K$ restricts to the comparison for $g=fj$. Here is the complete cancellation. Write $J_R=j_{!,R}$, $U_R=j_R^*$, and $v_R:J_RU_R\to1$ for the open counit, and let $a_U:T_UU_A\simeq U_BT_X$ be the restriction/tensor identification. By [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] and [det-sf-mate-open-restriction], the counit for $g$ is $\epsilon_{f,R}\,F_{f,R}(v_R G_{f,R})$. The canonical compact-support comparison is
$$b_g(N)=F_{f,B}(b_j(N))\,b_f(J_AN),$$
as follows by the transpose computation in Steps 8–10. After using $a_U$ to identify $T_UU_AG_AK$ with $U_BT_XG_AK$, the inverse transpose of $U_Bc_K$ under the composite adjunction is
$$\epsilon_{f,B}\,F_{f,B}(v_B G_B T_YK)\,F_{f,B}J_B(U_Bc_K)
=\epsilon_{f,B}\,F_{f,B}(c_K)\,F_{f,B}(v_B T_XG_AK),$$
by naturality of $v_B$. The defining equation of $c_K$ turns this into
$$T_Y\epsilon_{f,A}\;b_f(G_AK)^{-1}\;F_{f,B}(v_B T_XG_AK).$$
Step 8's open-counit scalar equality is an equality on the ordinary etale site; the pro-etale open adjunction $J_R\dashv U_R$ is its transport by [det-sp-et-proet-adjunction-transfer] (Step 4 applied to $j$, all objects having etale origin by Step 3), and the first square of [lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility] carries the identity with $\beta_j$ to the same identity with $b_j$. So on the pro-etale site
$$v_B T_XG_AK=T_X(v_A G_AK)\,b_j(U_AG_AK)^{-1}.$$
Naturality of $b_f$ now rewrites the preceding inverse transpose as
$$T_Y\epsilon_{f,A}\;T_YF_{f,A}(v_A G_AK)\;b_f(J_AU_AG_AK)^{-1}\;F_{f,B}(b_j(U_AG_AK)^{-1})
=T_Y(\epsilon_{g,A,K})\,b_g(U_AG_AK)^{-1}.$$
This is exactly the inverse transpose defining $c_{g,K}$; hence $j^*c_K=c_{g,K}$. Step 11 says the canonical $a_{g,K}$ has this same inverse transpose, so uniqueness gives $j^*c_K=a_{g,K}$, the required chart identification and an isomorphism. Here the composition square of [lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility] for the pair $(j,f)$, after the $\alpha_A,\alpha_B$ identifications, is exactly the displayed formula $b_g=F_{f,B}(b_j)b_f(J_A-)$. Its refinement square identifies this formula with the comparison for the fixed compactification of $g$, so the final inverse transpose is the named one defining $c_{g,K}$.

source.place: Locality and Charts: identify the restricted transpose

proof.text: Smooth local normal form [sbc-thm-etale-local-normal-form] gives coordinate charts after replacing the base and source by affine neighborhoods. Compose its etale map to $\mathbf A^d_V$ with the open immersion $\mathbf A^d_V\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^d_Y$; this is an etale chart over $Y$. Pure relative dimension fixes its dimension to $d$. The affine neighborhoods cover $X$. They are Noetherian, as are $X,Y$ and their affine spaces, by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Open subschemes remain Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian], so the chart open immersions are quasi-compact and are of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-qc-open-immersion-finite-type]. By [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1), the etale coordinate map from an affine source to the separated affine-space target is of finite presentation, hence finite type. It is separated: its relative diagonal is the base change of the closed diagonal of its separated $k$-source along $U\times_{\mathbf A^d_Y}U\to U\times_kU$, hence closed by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](b). Thus all these maps satisfy the hypotheses of the adjunctions used above. Step 12 makes every restriction of $c_K$ an isomorphism. Clause (3) of [det-sf-mate-open-restriction] detects isomorphisms on this open cover, and proves $c_K$ is an isomorphism globally. Only isomorphism detection is used here; no assertion that restriction is faithful on all derived morphisms is needed.

source.place: Locality: cover by charts and detection of isomorphisms
